warm-up 40 sent (1 failed), excluded from stats

a.B/One: at 50 rps, 48 of 150 calls (32.0%) got no answer within 300ms,
and nothing after the call sent at 6.0s of the run got one.
30 of them went out with less than half the timeout left: the target had
the smaller part of it.
a.B/One: 4 calls timed out before going out: they waited on the connection or the
generator, not the target.

failed calls by gRPC code:
a.B/One codes sent by the target: Unavailable 5
a.B/One codes set by the client: DeadlineExceeded 3

connections: 1; target stream limit 1.

not sent 4: waited for a stream 3, waited for the connection 1.

a.B/One: p99 without client-side waits (generator, connection, stream) is 100ms.

start lag, how late calls began against their schedule: p99 3.00ms, max 12.0ms.
It does not see answers picked up late.
Timeouts returned up to 7.00ms past their deadline.

The "request error" rows are calls that fail the same way at any rate. Either
the request is wrong - no such method, a bad argument, a body that does not match
the schema - or
a request refused as larger than accepted, by the target or a proxy in front of it.
Check the config for a.B/One.

A method's percentiles are the time to serve a call: successes, and timeouts
as lower bounds. The rows under it time the other answers:
"overload": the status says overloaded or unavailable (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED,
UNAVAILABLE), from the target or a proxy in front of it; a proxy with no live
backend says the same;
"failure": the status says the call broke (INTERNAL, UNKNOWN, ABORTED and
others), from the target or a proxy in front of it;
"bad response": a reply came and the client did not accept it.

50 requests were abandoned before answering. A percentile shown as "> value"
is a lower bound: the real tail lies above it. Raise the timeout to see it.

invalid run: calls held their slots more than 100ms (the allowance) past their
deadline, and the in-flight cap was hit at 1.2s. The generator lacked CPU, or the sender
does not honor deadlines; the target is not what filled the cap. At the hit 21 slots
were being held past their own deadline; 1 call was refused by the cap and
never sent.

incomplete: the run stopped before its planned end, and ran 10.0s of the planned 12.0s.
The numbers are honest but cover only the part that ran; do not compare them with a
full run.

limited by the run, not the target: on 1 connection the target allows 1 stream
(MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS), and 48 of 200 sent calls waited for one (p99 130ms), 3 more were not sent.
The printed p99 includes the wait for 1 of 1 methods. The target was not tested
above 1 call in flight.

3 calls were cut off after going out: no status came back, and the other end,
the target or a proxy in front of it, may have processed them.

2 requests never reached the target and carry no latency, so they are
counted as failures but left out of the percentiles above.

warning: 1 requests fell outside the per-second timeline and are missing
from it. The generator ran far behind its schedule or a clock jumped; the
totals above still count them.

warning: 1 requests came back without a category and are left out of the
percentiles. This is a bug in the sender, not in the target. Please report it.

warning: 2 measurements were impossible (negative latency) and left out.
This is a bug in LeetTest, not in the target. Please report it.
